answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token in a public escrow before it may submit bids or earn reputation. The contract releases the stake only after a dispute window; proven fraud burns it or pays challengers, while honest agents recover it. Splitting one agent into many identities then multiplies the capital tied up and the risk of loss, so a Sybil attack must fund every fake separately. Like an ocean current, reputation can wander across markets, but a glacier-slow stake release makes rapid identity cycling costly.
